scope: Bounded slice-4 delta only: Ordinary Bear, Ashcoat Bear, Owlbear, Soul Warden, Flash, Trample and another-creature-enters. This is not full issue-17, #16 integration, release or merge approval.

findings.summary: Soul Warden's 'Whenever another creature enters' trigger is queued only by enter_battlefield. create_tokens inserts creature tokens directly on the battlefield and queues only the token's own ETB trigger, so Soul Warden never triggers for Goblin/Drake creature tokens already supported by this pool.
findings.repro: aperture-cli selfplay --seed 1 --deck evidence/issue17/slice4/slice4-probe-warden.txt --deck evidence/issue17/slice4/slice4-probe-warden.txt --max-steps 3000 --verbose (deck: 10 Soul Warden, 10 Goblin Instigator, 10 Plains, 10 Mountain).
findings.observed: Log slice4-probe-warden-token.log: P0 casts Goblin Instigator; the Instigator entry queues Soul Warden; then 'state-based action: P0 creates Goblin Token token (#81)' immediately follows with no Soul Warden trigger for the token.
findings.expected: The token is another creature entering, so each Soul Warden controlled by P0/P1 should queue its life-gain trigger for that token exactly as for a nontoken ETB. Current tests cover self, opponent nontoken and noncreature exclusions but not the token path.
findings.required_repair: Share the AnotherCreatureEnters watcher-queue step between enter_battlefield and create_tokens (excluding the entering token itself), and add a token-entry regression.

Trample assigns lethal damage per blocker (toughness minus marked damage, minimum 1), carries surplus across blockers, then assigns only the remainder to the defending player; non-trample keeps all remaining damage on the last blocker. One-blocker and non-trample controls pass; multi-blocker and pre-damaged-blocker cases are code-consistent but not separately tested.
